title: Efficient Orthogonal Multi-view Subspace Clustering

problem.claim: Multi-view subspace clustering must cluster data lying in a union of low-dimensional subspaces, but conventional affinity-graph construction and spectral clustering become difficult to scale because they require quadratic or cubic time and space complexity.

gap.claim: Existing anchor-selection efforts pay little attention to the algebraic properties of anchors, and learning high-quality orthogonal bases while preserving scalability remains a challenge.

contributions.claim: An Efficient Orthogonal Multi-view Subspace Clustering model is proposed with almost linear complexity.

Anchor learning, graph construction, and graph partitioning are jointly modeled in a unified framework to jointly obtain a more discriminative and flexible anchor representation and cluster indicator.
An alternating minimization strategy is developed for the optimization problem, with claimed linear time complexity with respect to the number of samples.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments confirm the superiority of OMSC.
The authors report that source code and data are available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multi-view subspace clustering addresses data distributed across a union of low-dimensional subspaces.
Standard approaches construct an affinity graph and apply spectral clustering, but their quadratic or cubic time and space costs hinder large-scale clustering.
Prior anchor-based efforts do not sufficiently address anchor algebraic properties, leaving scalable learning of high-quality orthogonal bases unresolved.
OMSC jointly models anchor learning, graph construction, and partitioning, using mutual enhancement and alternating minimization to target almost-linear scalability.
The authors report extensive experiments and availability of source code and data.

source_observation.claim: The method jointly models anchor learning, graph construction, and partitioning.

interpretation.claim: Integrating coupled stages may allow their representations to improve one another instead of optimizing each stage independently.

application.claim: For scalable clustering pipelines, consider a unified objective when intermediate representations and final assignments mutually constrain each other.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when joint modeling is preferable to modular optimization or what trade-offs it introduces.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative experimental results.
The abstract does not provide the optimization formulation, orthogonality constraints, or detailed complexity derivation.
